title: ADHD among children and adults, with Margaret Sibley, PhD

sentences.en: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, or ADHD, was originally thought of as a disorder of childhood.
sentences.zh: 注意力缺陷多动障碍，也就是多动症（ADHD），最初被认为是一种儿童期疾病。

sentences.en: And for many people, the image that comes to mind when they think of ADHD is an 8-year-old boy who can't sit still in class.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，当他们想到多动症时，脑海中浮现的形象是一个8岁、在课堂上坐立不安的男孩。

sentences.en: But in recent decades, scientists have gained a more sophisticated understanding of the causes of ADHD
sentences.zh: 但在最近几十年里，科学家对多动症成因的理解变得更加深入，

sentences.en: and have begun to realize that it can be a lifelong disorder with lifelong consequences.
sentences.zh: 并开始意识到这可能是一种会伴随终身并产生终身影响的疾病。

sentences.en: Estimates of the prevalence of ADHD vary, but data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sentences.zh: 关于多动症发病率的估计各有不同，但来自疾病控制和预防中心的数据

sentences.en: found that in 2019, 8.8% of all children ages 3 to 17 had ever received a diagnosis of ADHD.
sentences.zh: 发现，在2019年，所有3至17岁的儿童中有8.8%曾被诊断患有多动症。

sentences.en: That prevalence has risen fairly steadily since the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 自20世纪90年代以来，这一发病率一直在相当稳步地上升。

sentences.en: How has our understanding of ADHD changed over those years?
sentences.zh: 多年来，我们对多动症的理解发生了怎样的变化？

sentences.en: What do we know about how it looks in childhood, adolescence, and adulthood?
sentences.zh: 对于它在儿童期、青春期和成年期的表现，我们了解多少？

sentences.en: Is it possible to develop ADHD as an adult?
sentences.zh: 成年后有可能患上多动症吗？

sentences.en: What are the most effective treatments?
sentences.zh: 最有效的治疗方法是什么？

sentences.en: And how has the pandemic affected children and adults with the disorder?
sentences.zh: 大流行又是如何影响患有这种疾病的儿童和成人的？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听“心理学对话”，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Maggie Sibley, a clinical psychologist at Seattle Children's Hospital
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是西雅图儿童医院的临床心理学家玛吉·西布利博士，

sentences.en: and an associate professor of psychiatry and behavioral sciences at the University of Washington School of Medicine.
sentences.zh: 她也是华盛顿大学医学院精神病学和行为科学副教授。

sentences.en: Dr. Sibley's work focuses on the diagnosis and treatment of ADHD in adolescents and young adults.
sentences.zh: 西布利博士的工作重点是青少年和年轻成人的多动症诊断与治疗。

sentences.en: She's developed a treatment therapy called STAND, Supporting Teens Autonomy Daily, to help teens with ADHD and their parents.
sentences.zh: 她开发了一种名为STAND（日常支持青少年自主性）的治疗疗法，以帮助患有多动症的青少年及其父母。

sentences.en: She's also co-authored more than 75 scientific papers on ADHD, including a recent study that found for most people diagnosed as children,
sentences.zh: 她还合著了75篇以上关于多动症的科学论文，其中包括最近的一项研究，该研究发现，对于大多数在儿童时期被诊断出的人来说，

sentences.en: ADHD symptoms continue into adulthood.
sentences.zh: 多动症的症状会持续到成年。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today, Dr. Sibley.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您今天能做客我们的节目，西布利博士。

sentences.en: I'm happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Let's start with the basics.
sentences.zh: 让我们从基础开始吧。

sentences.en: I mentioned in the introduction that many people have a mental image of a person with ADHD as a hyperactive young child, usually a boy, who can't pay attention in class.
sentences.zh: 我在导语中提到过，许多人对多动症患者的刻板印象是一个多动的小孩，通常是个男孩，在课堂上无法集中注意力。

sentences.en: But that's a very incomplete picture of ADHD.
sentences.zh: 但这对于多动症来说是一个非常不完整的画面。

sentences.en: Can you tell us a little more about what ADHD actually entails, how it's defined, and how it's diagnosed?
sentences.zh: 您能多给我们讲讲多动症实际上包含什么、它是如何定义的以及它是如何被诊断的吗？

sentences.en: So ADHD is a disorder with biological underpinnings, and we've done decades of research now that shows that there is a genetic component to ADHD for many people,
sentences.zh: 所以多动症是一种有生物学基础的疾病，几十年的研究表明，对许多人来说，多动症存在遗传因素，

sentences.en: and that the genes that seem to be related to ADHD are related to the chemical in the brain called dopamine.
sentences.zh: 并且似乎与多动症相关的基因与大脑中的一种名为多巴胺的化学物质有关。

sentences.en: And dopamine is a chemical in your brain that modulates your response to rewards.
sentences.zh: 多巴胺是你大脑中调节你对奖励反应的化学物质。

sentences.en: And so people with ADHD may have trouble regulating their attention, may have trouble being motivated, may have trouble with controlling their cognition,
sentences.zh: 因此，多动症患者可能在调节注意力、保持动力以及控制认知方面遇到困难，

sentences.en: because the chemical in their brain dopamine is working a little bit differently than it is for the average person.
sentences.zh: 因为他们大脑中的化学物质多巴胺的工作方式与常人略有不同。

sentences.en: And so in young children, you're going to see this translate into trouble controlling your behavior and hyperactivity and trouble paying attention in school
sentences.zh: 所以在幼童身上，你会看到这表现为难以控制自己的行为、多动以及在学校难以集中注意力。

sentences.en: But as people get older, you're going to see the symptoms of ADHD change a little bit.
sentences.zh: 但随着年龄的增长，你会发现多动症的症状会发生一些变化。

sentences.en: In adolescence, you're going to see the hyperactivity go down, and a lot more of the impairment has to do with your attention control
sentences.zh: 在青春期，你会发现多动现象减少了，更多的损伤与你的注意力控制有关，

sentences.en: and your ability to stay organized and stay motivated and overcome things like procrastination.
sentences.zh: 以及你保持条理、保持动力和克服拖延症等问题的能力。

sentences.en: And even in adulthood, the disorder changes even more, And you're going to see people struggle with things like staying on top of their finances,
sentences.zh: 甚至在成年期，这种疾病变化得更大，你会看到人们在处理财务等事情时挣扎，

sentences.en: being able to hold down a steady job, stay on task, being able to do work that sometimes isn't the most appealing and keep themselves motivated.
sentences.zh: 无法维持一份稳定的工作、专注于任务、无法完成有时并不那么吸引人的工作并保持自我动力。

sentences.en: So it's really that link of being able to control the way you think and the way you act that strings together what ADHD is across the lifespan.
sentences.zh: 因此，正是这种控制思考和行动方式的能力的联系，贯穿了多动症在整个生命周期中的表现。

sentences.en: So there are factors that have to be present, though, in order for somebody to get a real clinical diagnosis of ADHD.
sentences.zh: 不过，要让某人真正获得多动症的临床诊断，必须具备某些因素。

sentences.en: Can you talk about what those are?
sentences.zh: 您能谈谈这些因素是什么吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So in order to be diagnosed with ADHD, you have to show this pattern of behavior that is related to attention and motivation and cognitive control.
sentences.zh: 因此，要被诊断为多动症，你必须表现出与注意力、动机和认知控制相关的这种行为模式。

sentences.en: But at the same time, those difficulties have to be severe enough that they actually cause a real problem in a person's life.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，这些困难必须严重到在人们的生活中真正造成问题的程度。

sentences.en: So everyone may have tendencies to sometimes have trouble staying on task or focusing sometimes, but a person with ADHD is going to experience that in multiple settings.
sentences.zh: 因此，每个人有时都可能有难以保持专注或有时无法聚焦的倾向，但多动症患者会在多个环境中经历这种情况。

sentences.en: So whether it's at home and at work or at school and with social activities, you're going to see it in a pattern across your life.
sentences.zh: 无论是家里、工作场所、学校还是社交活动中，你都会在生活中看到这种模式。

sentences.en: And you're also going to see that impairment.
sentences.zh: 你还会看到这种损伤。

sentences.en: It's going to mean that you're going to have real problems in your life because of these symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 这意味着由于这些症状，你的生活中会遇到真正的问题。

sentences.en: It's going to be for people in school, their grades aren't as high as they could be.
sentences.zh: 对于学校里的人来说，他们的成绩没有达到应有的水平。

sentences.en: For people who have jobs, they might have trouble holding down the jobs.
sentences.zh: 对于有工作的人来说，他们可能很难保住工作。

sentences.en: Socially, you might find yourself with problematic relationships with other people
sentences.zh: 在社交方面，你可能会发现自己与他人的人际关系出现问题，

sentences.en: or difficulty holding down a romantic relationship because you're having trouble controlling your thoughts and your behaviors.
sentences.zh: 或者难以维持一段恋爱关系，因为你在控制自己的思想和行为方面遇到了困难。

sentences.en: You published a paper in August that found only about 10% of people diagnosed with ADHD as children will grow out of it as adults.
sentences.zh: 您在8月份发表了一篇论文，发现只有大约10%在儿童期被诊断患有多动症的人在成年后会克服它。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that research?
sentences.zh: 您能谈谈这项研究吗？

sentences.en: So I'm lucky to be a part of the multimodal treatment study of ADHD, which was a big study done in the 1990s where about 500 children with ADHD got different treatments,
sentences.zh: 我很荣幸能参与多动症多模式治疗研究，这是20世纪90年代进行的一项大型研究，其中大约500名患有多动症的儿童接受了不同的治疗，

sentences.en: medication treatments, behavioral treatments, and a little bit of both for some of the groups.
sentences.zh: 药物治疗、行为治疗，对于某些群体来说，两者结合了一点。

sentences.en: And then these children were followed until fairly recently, until they were about age 25.
sentences.zh: 然后这些儿童被追踪到相当晚近的时候，直到他们大约25岁。

sentences.en: And so we were able to, every two years or so, check in, find out what the symptoms and the functioning of these kids were like
sentences.zh: 因此，我们能够每两年左右回访一次，了解这些孩子的症状和功能表现如何，

sentences.en: by asking their parents, by asking their teachers, by asking themselves.
sentences.zh: 通过询问他们的父母、老师以及他们自己。

sentences.en: And with that really complete picture of how their ADHD was changing over time, what we saw was that there's only about 10% of this group of children
sentences.zh: 通过对他们的多动症随时间变化的真正完整的了解，我们看到这一群儿童中只有大约10%

sentences.en: who continue to steadily have a high level of ADHD all the way to age 25.
sentences.zh: 一直持续保持着高水平的多动症，直到25岁。

sentences.en: There's about another 10% who seem to have pretty steadily overcome their ADHD and stayed recovered.
sentences.zh: 大约还有10%的人似乎相当稳定地克服了他们的多动症并保持了康复状态。

sentences.en: And then most of the other people are somewhere in the middle where their ADHD seems to go up or down over time, depending on their circumstances.
sentences.zh: 然后其他大多数人则处于中间的某个位置，他们的多动症似乎会随着环境的变化而上下波动。

sentences.en: So there might be some years of their life where the ADHD actually looked more severe than other years.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们生命中的某些年份，多动症实际上可能看起来比其他年份更严重。

sentences.en: And if that's the case, that opens up a lot of questions about, well, what causes those fluctuations?
sentences.zh: 如果是这样的话，这就引发了很多问题：那么，是什么导致了这些波动？

sentences.en: And are we really surprised that most people are still struggling with ADHD long-term?
sentences.zh: 我们是否真的对大多数人长期以来仍在与多动症抗争感到惊讶？

sentences.en: I don't think so, because as a disorder with a biological underpinning that's chronic,
sentences.zh: 我认为并非如此，因为作为一种具有生物学基础的慢性疾病，

sentences.en: just like diabetes or anything else that you're born with that you kind of struggle with for your life, you wouldn't expect it to just go away,
sentences.zh: 就像你生来就要终生与之抗争的糖尿病或其他任何东西一样，你不会指望它凭空消失，

sentences.en: even though we can learn to manage it and have folks do a lot better.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们可以学会管理它并让患者做得更好。

sentences.en: And all the people in this study, were they in treatment at the time?
sentences.zh: 这项研究中的所有人，当时都在接受治疗吗？

sentences.en: Well, at the time of the study, they were given treatments as a part of the study.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在研究期间，他们作为研究的一部分接受了治疗。

sentences.en: And so they all got 14 months of treatment.
sentences.zh: 所以他们都接受了14个月的治疗。

sentences.en: And then after that, they no longer got treatments from the research team.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，他们不再接受研究团队的治疗。

sentences.en: But of course, many of them went and got treatment out in their communities, whether it was medication or seeing a psychologist and getting therapy.
sentences.zh: 但当然，他们中的许多人去社区寻求治疗，无论是药物治疗还是去看心理学家并接受心理治疗。

sentences.en: And so there's still an open question about what role treatment has in helping people overcome their symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，关于治疗在帮助人们克服症状方面发挥什么作用，仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。

sentences.en: But we do have evidence-based treatments for ADHD that do help people both in the short term and in the long term.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实有针对多动症的循证疗法，这些疗法确实在短期和长期内都能帮助人们。

sentences.en: So certainly that's a piece of the picture.
sentences.zh: 所以这肯定是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: Now, there's been a rise in recent years in the number of people being diagnosed with ADHD for the first time in adulthood.
sentences.zh: 现在，近年来首次在成年期被诊断为多动症的人数有所上升。

sentences.en: Is it possible to develop ADHD as an adult?
sentences.zh: 成年后有可能患上多动症吗？

sentences.en: Or did the people who are being diagnosed as adults probably have it as children, but just weren't diagnosed at the time?
sentences.zh: 还是说那些在成年期被诊断的人可能在童年时就有了，只是当时没有被诊断出来？

sentences.en: This is a really interesting question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: So first of all, we think there's a big group that I would call late-identified ADHD, which means they probably had ADHD or tendencies that are similar to ADHD the whole time.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们认为有一个很大的群体，我称之为晚期识别的多动症，这意味着他们可能一直都有多动症或类似多动症的倾向。

sentences.en: But for various reasons, they were not noticed until they were an adult and they were able to speak up for themselves.
sentences.zh: 但出于各种原因，直到他们成年并能够为自己发声之前，他们都没有被注意到。

sentences.en: And we already know some of the factors that can lead to that.
sentences.zh: 我们已经知道一些会导致这种情况的因素。

sentences.en: For example, ADHD is a lot less recognized in girls and women because they aren't so hyperactive and loud about their symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 例如，多动症在女孩和妇女中受到的认可要少得多，因为她们在症状上没有那么多动和吵闹。

sentences.en: And so sometimes people think that they're just a little bit spacey and they don't actually get the diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 所以有时人们认为她们只是有点神游，实际上并没有得到诊断。

sentences.en: We also know in people of color or people who might come from cultures where mental health difficulties are not recognized as mental health difficulties,
sentences.zh: 我们也知道，在有色人种或来自不将心理健康困难视为心理健康困难的文化背景的人群中，

sentences.en: that they may not come to the attention of professionals or be recognized as well.
sentences.zh: 他们可能不会引起专业人员的注意，也没有得到很好的识别。

sentences.en: So certainly better recognition in our school systems where educators are learning to keep their eyes out for kids who are struggling in this area
sentences.zh: 因此，我们的学校系统对教育工作者进行培训，让他们留心在这方面苦苦挣扎的孩子，这种认可的提高，

sentences.en: has helped us learn to see kids at an earlier age that may have ADHD.
sentences.zh: 确实帮助我们在更小的年龄发现可能患有多动症的孩子。

sentences.en: But still, we have a 3% rate of ADHD in adulthood overall.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，成年期多动症的总体发病率仍为3%。

sentences.en: And as you were saying, something like 8% in childhood.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，童年期约为8%。

sentences.en: So if you agree that ADHD is a chronic disorder, we're still missing a lot of people, even though maybe now we're capturing more people.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你承认多动症是一种慢性疾病，我们仍然漏掉了很多人，尽管也许现在我们捕捉到了更多的人。

sentences.en: Can it come on as an adult and never have any symptoms earlier?
sentences.zh: 它会在成年期发作而早期没有任何症状吗？

sentences.en: That's still a bit of a debated question.
sentences.zh: 这仍然是一个有争议的问题。

sentences.en: I think it depends on how you define ADHD.
sentences.zh: 我认为这取决于你如何定义多动症。

sentences.en: Because if you consider any difficulties with paying attention or focusing or controlling your behavior or your thoughts as a form of ADHD,
sentences.zh: 因为如果你把任何注意力不集中、专注困难或控制行为或思想的困难都视为多动症的一种形式，

sentences.en: you might be able to say yes, because we know things like going through trauma or things like having experiences,
sentences.zh: 你或许可以说“是”，因为我们知道经历创伤或经历某些事情，

sentences.en: maybe even where you were involved with substances and then you stopped, can impact your cognition in ways that look like ADHD.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能涉及物质滥用然后停止的经历，都会以看起来像多动症的方式影响你的认知。

sentences.en: There's a lot of ADHD mimics out there.
sentences.zh: 外面有很多长得像多动症的“模仿者”。

sentences.en: And so it's really important when people are getting diagnosed as adults that they go to a professional who can tell the difference
sentences.zh: 因此，当成年人接受诊断时，去找一个能分清以下情况的专业人员非常重要：

sentences.en: between kind of our classic ADHD that has that biological underpinning and starts in childhood
sentences.zh: 一种是具有生物学基础并始于童年的经典多动症，

sentences.en: and something else that has similar symptoms but might have a different source of where it came from.
sentences.zh: 另一种是症状相似但来源可能不同的其他情况。

sentences.en: So speaking of prevalence, there's an idea out there that's been around for years that ADHD is overdiagnosed
sentences.zh: 说到发病率，有一个流传多年的观点认为多动症被过度诊断了，

sentences.en: and that some children are given medication when they don't really need it.
sentences.zh: 一些儿童在并不真正需要时被开了药物。

sentences.en: I mean, isn't it just the nature of childhood that some kids are rambunctious and have trouble paying attention in school?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有些孩子精力旺盛并且在学校难以集中注意力，这难道不是童年的天性吗？

sentences.en: And mightn't it be a case of overworked and overburdened parents who want something to control their children because they can't do it themselves?
sentences.zh: 这会不会是那些工作过度、不堪重负的父母，因为自己管教不了孩子，所以想要某种东西来控制他们的情况？

sentences.en: Are these valid concerns?
sentences.zh: 这些是合理的担忧吗？

sentences.en: I like to say that ADHD is misdiagnosed, not over or underdiagnosed.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢说多动症是被误诊了，而不是过度诊断或诊断不足。

sentences.en: Because like we just talked about, there are some people who are being missed and there are also some people who may be being given a diagnosis somewhat liberally.
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们刚才所讨论的，有些人被漏诊了，同时也有一些人可能在某种程度上被随意地给予了诊断。

sentences.en: And I think that that is up to any individual provider about how confident they are when they make an ADHD diagnosis
sentences.zh: 我认为这取决于每个提供者在做出多动症诊断时的自信程度，

sentences.en: and how severe a symptom presentation that provider feels they need to see in order to give the diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 以及为了给出诊断，提供者觉得需要看到多大程度的症状表现。

sentences.en: So I definitely think there are individuals somewhere out there who are probably given a liberal diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 所以我绝对认为在某些地方确实有人可能得到了比较随意的诊断。

sentences.en: On the other hand, I don't think that's an overwhelming trend of most people who have ADHD were given a diagnosis that's a stretch.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我认为这并不是绝大多数患有多动症的人被勉强诊断的压倒性趋势。

sentences.en: I think one of the places we have to be most careful is when there's an incentive to have an ADHD diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们必须最谨慎的地方之一是存在获得多动症诊断的动机时。

sentences.en: And so you can see this in college students, for example, who I think in the last 10 to 15 years,
sentences.zh: 例如，你可以在大学生身上看到这一点，我认为在过去10到15年里，

sentences.en: we've seen this growth in college students who are pretty strategic, who go to the right provider
sentences.zh: 我们看到这种大学生群体在增长，他们相当有策略性，会去找合适的提供者，

sentences.en: and are able to get a prescription for a stimulant medication, which will help anyone study.
sentences.zh: 并能够获得兴奋剂药物的处方，这可以帮助任何人学习。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter if you have ADHD or not, right?
sentences.zh: 不管你有没有多动症，对吧？

sentences.en: So that doesn't necessarily drive up our rates of ADHD diagnosis in the country alone,
sentences.zh: 所以这不一定单单推高了我们国家的多动症诊断率，

sentences.en: but there are certain subgroups where providers have to be careful and be very thorough when they're diagnosing because people may have ulterior motives for getting that diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 但在某些子群体中，提供者在诊断时必须小心并且非常彻底，因为人们可能有获得该诊断的别有用心的动机。

sentences.en: So you mentioned medication as one of the treatment options.
sentences.zh: 所以你提到药物治疗是治疗选择之一。

sentences.en: What are the various options that are available and are they different depending on age for children, for adolescents, for adults?
sentences.zh: 都有哪些不同的选择？对于儿童、青少年和成人，这些选择根据年龄会有所不同吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, overall, there's two categories of treatment.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，总的来说，治疗分为两大类。

sentences.en: So one is the medications.
sentences.zh: 一种是药物治疗。

sentences.en: Most of them are stimulant medications, though there are some non-stimulants.
sentences.zh: 大多数是兴奋剂药物，尽管也有一些非兴奋剂药物。

sentences.en: And then you're going to have your psychological treatments, which are, it's a CBT-like model in adults,
sentences.zh: 然后是你的心理治疗，对于成年人来说，这是一种类似CBT（认知行为疗法）的模型，

sentences.en: and obviously when you're with younger children, it's going to be more of a behavior therapy, parent training-like model.
sentences.zh: 显然，当你面对更小的儿童时，它会更偏向于行为疗法、家长培训类的模型。

sentences.en: But these two types of treatments do very different things.
sentences.zh: 但这两种类型的治疗发挥着非常不同的作用。

sentences.en: So if you take a medication while it's in your system, it is going to directly intervene on that chemical dopamine,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你服用了药物，在其在你体内起效期间，它将直接干预化学物质多巴胺，

sentences.en: and it's going to directly help your cognition feel more under control.
sentences.zh: 并且它将直接帮助你的认知感觉受到更多控制。

sentences.en: So if somebody hasn't taken a stimulant medication and they're curious what it feels like,
sentences.zh: 所以如果有人没有服用过兴奋剂药物，并且好奇那是什么感觉，

sentences.en: it would be like having a really good cup of coffee with none of the jitters and none of the side effects, right?
sentences.zh: 那就像喝了一杯非常棒的咖啡，没有任何心神不宁，也没有任何副作用，对吧？

sentences.en: You have the focus ability without the profile of things that kind of feel uncomfortable when you start giving yourself a stimulant.
sentences.zh: 你拥有专注能力，却没有那种当你开始给自己使用兴奋剂时让人感到不太舒服的症状谱。

sentences.en: So if you can imagine that that helps people focus better and can control their cognition,
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象，这可以帮助人们更好地集中注意力并控制他们的认知，

sentences.en: but as soon as it wears off, the person is back to their normal self, still experiencing those ADHD symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 但一旦药效过去，这个人就会恢复正常状态，依然经历着那些多动症症状。

sentences.en: The cognitive behavioral treatments are going to work on a couple things.
sentences.zh: 认知行为治疗则会从几个方面起作用。

sentences.en: Teaching people coping skills, so strategies for how they can stay organized.
sentences.zh: 教给人们应对技巧，即如何保持条理的策略。

sentences.en: And when we're working with the parents of the younger kids, it's teaching the parents to set up routines and create situations that help people with ADHD function their beSt.
sentences.zh: 当我们与较小孩子的父母合作时，它是教父母建立常规并创造有助于多动症患者发挥最佳功能的状况。

sentences.en: And then also helping people with ADHD identify areas in their life that they might be able to be successful,
sentences.zh: 然后还要帮助多动症患者识别生活中他们可能获得成功的领域，

sentences.en: what kinds of environments or settings are most conducive to them avoiding the impact of their symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 什么样的环境或背景最有利于他们避开症状带来的影响。

sentences.en: So whether that is for an adult, young adult, maybe trying to figure out what kind of educational or career path they want to go into,
sentences.zh: 因此，无论是对于成年人还是年轻成人，可能在试图弄清楚他们想走什么样的教育或职业道路时，

sentences.en: they might recognize that, you know what, I do best when I'm active, when I'm outside, when I'm working with my hands, I don't do as well sitting at a computer.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会认识到，你知道吗，当我活跃、在户外、用双手工作时，我表现得最好；坐在电脑前，我表现得没那么好。

sentences.en: And so helping people kind of get that self-awareness and make decisions to help them succeed.
sentences.zh: 因此，帮助人们建立这种自我意识并做出有助于他们成功的决定。

sentences.en: So both of those classes of treatments are effective.
sentences.zh: 所以这两类治疗都是有效的。

sentences.en: They help in complementary ways.
sentences.zh: 它们以互补的方式提供帮助。

sentences.en: I'm a big fan of doing both or trying both to sort of see how they can go hand in hand for an individual person.
sentences.zh: 我非常赞成两者都做或两者都尝试，以便看看它们如何能为一个具体的人齐头并进。

sentences.en: And ultimately, though, there's no right way to decide to get treated.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，决定如何接受治疗并没有唯一正确的方法。

sentences.en: Both of those options can be very helpful.
sentences.zh: 这两种选择都非常有用。

sentences.en: So some children are diagnosed as early as three years old,
sentences.zh: 所以有些儿童早在三岁时就被诊断出来了，

sentences.en: which leads me to the question of what's the earliest age at which it's considered to give any of these medications to children?
sentences.zh: 这让我想到了一个问题：给儿童使用这些药物的最小年龄是多少？

sentences.en: So there's guidelines out there for giving medication to preschoolers, and that's about as young as you'll see it done.
sentences.zh: 目前有一些针对学龄前儿童用药的指导方针，这差不多就是你能看到的最小用药年龄了。

sentences.en: There's a lot of controversy out there about that.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，外界存在很多争议。

sentences.en: I'm not a pediatrician, but I work with pediatricians, and I think a lot of pediatricians even feel uncomfortable giving that medication
sentences.zh: 我不是儿科医生，但我与儿科医生共事，我认为很多儿科医生甚至对使用这些药物感到不安，

sentences.en: and will refer to a psychiatrist or a specialist to really be careful before making a decision like that for a young child.
sentences.zh: 并且在为幼儿做出这样的决定之前，会咨询精神科医生或专科医生以确保万无一失。

sentences.en: And I think one of the big reasons for that is because disruptive and hyperactive behavior is somewhat normative at that young age,
sentences.zh: 我想其中一个主要原因在于，破坏性和多动行为在这个幼小的年龄段某种程度上是正常的，

sentences.en: and so it's really hard to tell the difference between somebody who's just a three-year-old and somebody who's actually got a chronic disorder.
sentences.zh: 因此很难区分一个人只是一个三岁小孩，还是确实患有慢性疾病。

sentences.en: And so there's a lot of caution in just not wanting to misgive the stimulant medication.
sentences.zh: 所以大家在避免错误使用兴奋剂药物方面非常谨慎。

sentences.en: It's not because we think stimulant medication is harmful at that age.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为我们认为兴奋剂药物在这个年龄段是有害的。

sentences.en: So you can diagnose ADHD in preschoolers, but I think there's less stability in that diagnosis when it's given that young
sentences.zh: 所以你可以在学龄前儿童身上诊断出ADHD，但我认为这么小的时候做出诊断，其稳定性较差，

sentences.en: because it's hard developmentally to decide who has it and who doesn't.
sentences.zh: 因为从发育角度来看，很难界定谁患有此症，谁没有。

sentences.en: And then what do we know about the long-term effects of taking these medications?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们对长期服用这些药物的副作用了解多少？

sentences.en: So if you start taking Adderall or whatever one of these medications might be as a child, how likely is it that you will have to take it for the rest of your life,
sentences.zh: 如果你在儿童时期开始服用阿德拉（Adderall）或诸如此类的药物，你余生都需要服用的可能性有多大，

sentences.en: and what do we know about what that might do to you physiologically?
sentences.zh: 我们又对这在生理上可能对你产生的影响了解多少？

sentences.en: There's no definitive answer on this at all, but there's two areas of research ongoing and possible speculation on this.
sentences.zh: 对此目前完全没有定论，但有两个正在进行的研究领域和可能的推测方向。

sentences.en: The first is on growth.
sentences.zh: 第一个是关于生长发育。

sentences.en: So there is some evidence from some of the longitudinal studies that if you take stimulant medication for a prolonged period of time, it could affect your growth.
sentences.zh: 一些纵向研究表明，如果长期服用兴奋剂药物，可能会影响生长发育。

sentences.en: This makes sense, right?
sentences.zh: 这很好理解，对吧？

sentences.en: Because the stimulant medications have a direct effect on appetite suppression,
sentences.zh: 因为兴奋剂药物对抑制食欲有直接作用，

sentences.en: and so kids who are taking stimulant medications for most of the days of the year are getting less food intake,
sentences.zh: 所以一年中大部分时间都在服用兴奋剂药物的孩子摄入的食物较少，

sentences.en: and therefore that's less nutrients, and therefore they're not growing as tall and as big as the kids who are not on these medications.
sentences.zh: 因此营养也较少，导致他们长得没有那些不服药的孩子那么高、那么壮。

sentences.en: So there's evidence that you can recover that growth somewhat by just not taking the medications over the summer, for example, or possibly taking holidays on the weekend.
sentences.zh: 有证据表明，比如通过在夏天停药，或者周末偶尔停药，在一定程度上可以恢复生长发育。

sentences.en: But also we're talking about in some of these studies like less than 2 centimeters of adult height being impacted.
sentences.zh: 但我们也注意到，其中一些研究显示成年后的身高受影响不到2厘米。

sentences.en: So do people care about that level of growth?
sentences.zh: 那么人们会在意这种程度的身高影响吗？

sentences.en: That's an open question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个开放性的问题。

sentences.en: Some people may and some people may not.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能会在意，有些人则不会。

sentences.en: So that's one area.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个方面。

sentences.en: It's still a little controversial because some of the findings are mixed, but something is probably there with that.
sentences.zh: 这仍然存在一些争议，因为部分研究结果并不一致，但其中确实存在某种影响。

sentences.en: The other area is whether or not people somehow are going to be more interested in using substances or drugs as adults because they took this medication as children.
sentences.zh: 另一个领域是，因为小时候服用过这种药物，成年后是否更有可能对物质或药物产生依赖。

sentences.en: And so there's been work investigating that, and overall it suggests that no, that is not the case.
sentences.zh: 为此开展了相关研究，总体表明：并没有，事实并非如此。

sentences.en: If people take stimulant medications as children, it does not make them more likely to want to use drugs as adults.
sentences.zh: 如果在儿童时期服用兴奋剂药物，并不会让他们在成年后更有吸毒的倾向。

sentences.en: So, you know, that I think is pretty thoroughly researched.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这已经得到了相当彻底的研究。

sentences.en: There is work investigating the idea of tolerance in ADHD medications.
sentences.zh: 还有研究探讨了ADHD药物的耐受性问题。

sentences.en: The idea that if you take medications for ADHD for a while, they start to wear off how effective they are on you.
sentences.zh: 也就是如果你服用ADHD药物一段时间后，它们对你的药效开始减弱的现象。

sentences.en: And there is some evidence to suggest that may happen and that it may be one of the main reasons why people with ADHD,
sentences.zh: 有证据表明这种情况可能会发生，这可能是ADHD患者的主要原因之一，

sentences.en: after several years, start wanting to stop taking them because they may not feel like they help as much as they used to do.
sentences.zh: 他们在几年后开始想要停药，因为他们觉得这些药不像以前那么管用了。

sentences.en: And this is an interesting research question that people are still looking at,
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的课题，人们仍在进行研究，

sentences.en: whether it has to do with the fact that it's a ratio of how much you weigh to how much of the pill you take and how many milligrams of the chemical you put in your body.
sentences.zh: 探讨这是否与体重和药丸剂量的比例有关，以及你身体里摄入了多少毫克的化学成分。

sentences.en: And as people grow up, technically you need to take more and more to keep the ratio of how much you weigh to how much chemical in balance.
sentences.zh: 随着人们长高长大，从技术上讲，你需要服用越来越多的药量，才能保持体重和化学成分的比例平衡。

sentences.en: But we have limits in the country about how big of doses we give people.
sentences.zh: 但我们国家对给人们服用的最大剂量有限制。

sentences.en: So, there is also kind of this concern of people developing over time kind of a tolerance to the medication.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们也担心随着时间推移，对药物产生某种程度的耐受性。

sentences.en: And can you keep upping the dose to keep the medication working?
sentences.zh: 那么，你能不能通过不断增加剂量来维持药效呢？

sentences.en: And at some point, maybe you can't.
sentences.zh: 但在某些时候，你可能做不到了。

sentences.en: So, it could be the case that we can't really see a good effect of medication for decades and decades
sentences.zh: 因此，几十年来我们可能真的看不到药物的良好效果，

sentences.en: because eventually someone hits a ceiling where, you know, its effects are lessened.
sentences.zh: 因为最终人们会达到一个瓶颈，其药效会减弱。

sentences.en: Research has shown that people with ADHD are at risk for a number of bad outcomes in their lives and co-occurring disorders such as depression, addiction, and even suicide.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，ADHD患者在生活中面临着许多不良结局的风险，并伴有抑郁、成瘾甚至自杀等共病。

sentences.en: Why is that and how can treatment help?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么？治疗又该如何提供帮助？

sentences.en: Well, ADHD is one of the biggest risk factors, like you say, for a lot of different negative outcomes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如你所说，ADHD是导致许多不同负面结局的最大风险因素之一。

sentences.en: And if you think about it, people with ADHD have trouble with self-control as sort of the main feature of their disorder.
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细想想，ADHD患者难以进行自我控制，这是他们疾病的主要特征。

sentences.en: So, they're going to have trouble sometimes with decision-making carefully.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们在做出谨慎决策时有时会遇到困难。

sentences.en: They also have trouble with risky behaviors because they have trouble with delaying their gratification and being patient for things.
sentences.zh: 他们还容易进行冒险行为，因为他们在延迟满足和保持耐心方面存在困难。

sentences.en: And if they want something, sometimes they don't think about the consequences and they just go for it.
sentences.zh: 如果他们想要什么，有时不会考虑后果，就会直接去做。

sentences.en: So, you see some risky behavior going on there.
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到其中存在一些冒险行为。

sentences.en: Another potential mechanism of this is people with ADHD unfortunately experience a lot of negative experiences in their life
sentences.zh: 另一个潜在机制是，ADHD患者不幸在生活中经历了许多负面体验，

sentences.en: because they aren't as good at school as other kids sometimes.
sentences.zh: 因为有时他们在学校里不如其他孩子表现好。

sentences.en: They don't have as many friends.
sentences.zh: 他们的朋友没那么多。

sentences.en: And they start to feel kind of bad about themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们开始对自我产生不好的看法。

sentences.en: They're getting a lot of negative feedback about the environment.
sentences.zh: 他们从周围环境中收到了很多负面反馈。

sentences.en: And so, that can help or that can lead to the development of self-esteem issues and other difficulties that can lead to things like depression and anxiety.
sentences.zh: 因此，这会促成或导致自尊问题以及其他困难的产生，进而引发抑郁和焦虑等问题。

sentences.en: So, you can see there's sort of like a cocktail brewing here where not only do you have your ADHD symptoms,
sentences.zh: 你可以看到，这里就像是在酿造一杯鸡尾酒，你不仅有ADHD的症状，

sentences.en: but some of the life experiences that come as a result of your ADHD symptoms create additional probleMs.
sentences.zh: 而且由ADHD症状带来的一些生活经历又产生了额外的问题。

sentences.en: And it kind of can snowball for people if they don't get on the right track and have the right supports in their life.
sentences.zh: 如果人们没有走上正轨并在生活中获得正确的支持，情况就会像滚雪球一样越来越糟。

sentences.en: And a big part of getting people treated when they're kids, when they're teenagers, even when they're adults,
sentences.zh: 让人们在儿童时期、青少年时期甚至是成年后接受治疗的一个重要部分，

sentences.en: is to help people kind of be aware of those risks and help them make good decisions to stay away from them.
sentences.zh: 就是帮助人们意识到这些风险，并帮助他们做出明智的决定以远离这些风险。

sentences.en: That makes a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 这非常在理。

sentences.en: So, it's not ADHD itself.
sentences.zh: 所以，这并非ADHD本身的问题。

sentences.en: It's the reaction to it by the community at large, if you will.
sentences.zh: 可以说是整个社会社区对它的反应。

sentences.en: That's definitely a factor.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一个因素。

sentences.en: So, now that awareness is growing that ADHD can be a lifelong disorder, are there resources out there for adults who suspect that they might have it?
sentences.zh: 那么，既然人们越来越认识到ADHD可能是一种终身疾病，对于怀疑自己可能患有此病的成年人来说，有哪些资源可供利用？

sentences.en: Where should adults go to get information?
sentences.zh: 成年人应该去哪里获取信息？

sentences.en: Well, I think the best public resource out there is the CHAD website for children and adults with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为最好的公共资源是CHADD网站，即注意力缺陷多动障碍儿童和成人协会。

sentences.en: This is one of the advocacy organizations for ADHD that is partnered with the Center for Disease Control, CDC, on getting good information out there for folks.
sentences.zh: 这是ADHD的倡导组织之一，它与疾病控制和预防中心（CDC）合作，为大众提供优质信息。

sentences.en: So, if you're wondering if you have ADHD or if you want to find out more about the disorder and what it's like and what your options are,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想知道自己是否患有ADHD，或者想更多地了解这种疾病、它的表现以及你的治疗选择，

sentences.en: definitely check out the CHAD, C-H-A-D-D, website.
sentences.zh: 一定要去看看CHADD（C-H-A-D-D）网站。

sentences.en: And that's a great starting place.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极佳的起点。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So, of course, in every podcast lately, we have to ask a question related to the pandemic, and here's yours.
sentences.zh: 当然，最近每期播客我们都得问一个与大流行相关的问题，这就是你的问题。

sentences.en: There have been a number of news articles in the past year that indicate that the pandemic has caused an uptick in ADHD diagnoses
sentences.zh: 过去一年里有许多新闻报道指出，大流行导致ADHD诊断率上升，

sentences.en: and parents seeking information about ADHD because of school disruptions and having their kids in the house all day.
sentences.zh: 由于学校停课以及孩子们整天在家，家长们纷纷寻求有关ADHD的信息。

sentences.en: Does this track with what you've been seeing in your clinical research and in your practice?
sentences.zh: 这与你在临床研究和实践中看到的情况相符吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全相符。

sentences.en: So, think about this.
sentences.zh: 所以，想想看。

sentences.en: ADHD is on a continuum, which means there are some people who clearly have very severe ADHD,
sentences.zh: ADHD是一个连续谱，这意味着有些人显然患有非常严重的ADHD，

sentences.en: and there are other people who might have a mild version of ADHD or even just tendencies towards ADHD
sentences.zh: 而另一些人可能患有轻度ADHD，或者仅仅具有ADHD的倾向，

sentences.en: that could potentially get exacerbated or worsened if the right conditions are in place.
sentences.zh: 在条件合适的情况下，这种倾向可能会被加剧或恶化。

sentences.en: And one of the conditions, especially for kids and teens who might be a little inattentive
sentences.zh: 其中一个条件，特别是对于那些可能有点注意力不集中，

sentences.en: or have a little trouble with organization and procrastination, would be losing the structure of your school day
sentences.zh: 或在组织能力和拖延症方面有点困难的儿童和青少年来说，就是失去了学校日常生活的结构，

sentences.en: and just being in one stationary place all day in front of a computer, you know,
sentences.zh: 整天坐在一台电脑前呆在同一个固定地方，你知道的，

sentences.en: trying to get your work done without the support of a teacher or the ability to interact with other kids in a physical way.
sentences.zh: 在没有老师的支持或无法与其他孩子进行实体互动的情况下努力完成学业。

sentences.en: And so, those conditions, I think, have led many people with milder ADHD to see more severe symptoms than they're usually having,
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为这些情况导致许多患有轻度ADHD的人出现了比平时更严重的症状，

sentences.en: and that's brought them to clinical attention where before maybe they wouldn't have been.
sentences.zh: 从而引起了临床关注，而在此之前他们可能不会受到关注。

sentences.en: And so, we have been seeing, you know, I've seen it both in the research and also clinically, more people coming in wondering if they, you know, could benefit from medication
sentences.zh: 所以我们一直看到，你知道的，我在研究和临床中都看到，越来越多的人前来询问他们是否能从药物中受益，

sentences.en: and particularly seeking out services for ADHD during this time.
sentences.zh: 并且在这期间特别寻求针对ADHD的服务。

sentences.en: So, last question.
sentences.zh: 那么最后一个问题。

sentences.en: What do you think are the biggest open questions about ADHD right now?
sentences.zh: 你认为目前关于ADHD最大的未解之谜是什么？

sentences.en: And as a result, what are you working on in your research?
sentences.zh: 因此，你目前在研究中致力于解决什么问题？

sentences.en: I think one of the biggest open questions is how do we get treatments that are effective out there to people who really need them, especially people in low-resource situations,
sentences.zh: 我认为最大的未解之谜之一，是如何将有效的治疗方法提供给真正需要的人，尤其是资源匮乏环境中的人，

sentences.en: kids who maybe, you know, experience various adversities.
sentences.zh: 比如那些可能经历各种逆境的孩子。

sentences.en: And so, if you have ADHD and you have adversity in your life, you're probably, you know, doubly, you know, struggling.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你患有ADHD并且生活中遭遇逆境，你可能正在遭受双重挣扎。

sentences.en: And so, it's been a disorder that, you know, people who regularly go into their pediatrician
sentences.zh: 一直以来，那些定期去看儿科医生，

sentences.en: or have the resources to go see a private psychologist have always been able to access care for.
sentences.zh: 或者有资源去看私人心理学家的患者，总是能够获得这种疾病的治疗护理。

sentences.en: But, you know, I do a lot of work in public schools and community mental health centers
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我在公立学校和社区心理健康中心做了很多工作，

sentences.en: trying to see how we could train folks to be able to do effective treatments, you know, in lower-resource ways.
sentences.zh: 试图探讨如何培训相关人员，以便能够以资源较少的方式开展有效的治疗。

sentences.en: Because I think prevention is everything with this disorder.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为对于这种疾病来说，预防就是一切。

sentences.en: If you can control the symptoms early, you do avoid a lot of those negative outcomes.
sentences.zh: 如果你能早期控制症状，你确实可以避免许多不良结局。

sentences.en: I also think another piece of the puzzle is a bigger focus on the environmental factors that can lead the symptoms to go up or down.
sentences.zh: 我还认为，拼图的另一块是更加关注能导致症状加剧或减轻的环境因素。

sentences.en: Because if we could identify factors that can help people's symptoms stay at bay or, you know, at least partially remitted in a subclinical range,
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们能找出有助于将人们的症状控制住，或者至少使其在亚临床范围内部分缓解的因素，

sentences.en: then we potentially can make interventions that can help harness those factors.
sentences.zh: 我们就有可能制定出利用这些因素的干预措施。

sentences.en: So, we need to be, you know, getting more interviews in and more research experiences in with people with ADHD to find the patterns in their life of when they feel they do well
sentences.zh: 因此，我们需要对ADHD患者进行更多的访谈和研究体验，以找出他们生活中感觉自己状态良好的规律，

sentences.en: and then leveraging that for people.
sentences.zh: 然后为大众加以利用。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for joining me today, Dr. Sibley.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你今天作客我们的节目，西布利博士。

sentences.en: I'm sure that our listeners are going to find your insights very, very helpful.
sentences.zh: 我相信我们的听众会觉得你的见解非常非常有帮助。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.zh: 您可以在 www.speakingofpsychology.org 或在 Apple、Stitcher、Spotify 或您获取喜爱的播客的任何地方找到《心理学聊天》往期节目。
